newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia cocoa tracks NY fall, harvest ends.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia cocoa tracks NY fall, harvest ends.

text.p: Indonesian cocoa prices were lower on Wednesday from a week ago at the end of the mid-crop harvest, and in line with falls in New York, traders said.
They said cocoa was quoted at 2,740-2,760 rupiah/kg in Ujung Pandang, capital of the key growing region of South Sulawesi, compared with 2,800-2,820 rupiah last week.
"The mid-crop harvest is over and there's not much beans around," one trader said. "Some players are trying to push up prices, but their motive is not clear."
He said trading was expected to remain dull until the start of the main crop harvest in April.
Another trader said heavy rains in some parts of South Sulawesi had affected flowering, but added that it was not widespread or expected to have any serious impact on the crop.
He also discounted market talk that there could be delay in the main crop harvest because of the rains.
"There have been some impact on the flowering process, but I don't think it is serious," he said. "I think the harvest will be on schedule."
Cocoa futures posted losses for the third straight session on Tuesday in New York, pressured by trade selling.
